meta.name: Combat visuals manifest
meta.purpose: Maps combat context (and, from ticket 09, enemy/ally template key) to the art asset that renders it, so scenes/screens/combat.gd never hardcodes a path. See docs/combat-animation-vision.md §2.1/§6 and docs/ART-BIBLE.md.
meta.backdropRule: One entry per Combat.CANONICAL_CONTEXTS context (systems/combat.gd). 'image' is a res:// path to a 390x360 backdrop plate, or "" when no plate has been produced yet -- the stage then fills with the flat data/palette.json colour named by 'fallbackColor' instead.
meta.templateRule: Ticket 09: 'templates' keys other than 'default' are the seven cast subjects (docs/combat-animation-vision.md §3) resolved by CombatScreen.enemy_template_key()/display-entry building -- 'player' (state.player), the recruited-ally contactId (e.g. 'archie'), the data/enemies.json raidGuards key (territorialScrapper/veinGuard/orichalchumDealer), 'homeRaidRaider' (GameData.ENEMY_HOME_RAID_RAIDER), and 'mugger' (any enemy with isMugging true, however many concurrent instances -- one sheet, reused). Each subject's 'idle' entry is {image, frameCount, fps}; an empty 'image' means no art has been produced yet -- CombatScreen.StageSlot falls back cleanly to the ticket-01 placeholder box, per-subject, not an error. 'default' is unrelated to this per-subject idle lookup -- it's ticket 10's own shared stand-in for attack/hit/ko only, untouched by ticket 09.
meta.actionRule: Ticket 10, docs/combat-animation-vision.md §4: 'attack' (3 keyposes: wind-up/strike/recover, played with a transform lunge-and-return), 'hit' (1 pose, played with a transform recoil), and 'ko' (2 poses, played with a transform fall+fade) exist per-subject exactly like 'idle' -- CombatScreen loads whichever of a sheet's frames the doctrine calls for (down-sampling evenly if a sheet carries more, e.g. templates.default's own multi-frame stand-in strips) and falls back to templates.default's shared stand-in when a subject's own entry is empty, same two-level fallback 'idle' would use if it had one. 'tell' (1 pose, held with a pulse) is ticket 06's telegraph slot getting real art instead of its text/glyph placeholder -- read directly, no default fallback (no enemy has a non-null `ability` in data/enemies.json yet, so no tell art has anywhere to point). 'selfPatch' is Archie-only (§3: the `_allies_act`/`_ally_turn` heal-below-40%-HP pose) -- also no default fallback, since a generic combat stand-in has no heal pose to lend. attack/hit/ko 'fps' values here (5.0/5.0/3.0) are deliberately much lower than idle's -- they pace a short keypose sequence (3/2/2 steps after down-sampling), not a dense flipbook, and were tuned so the total on-screen time per one-shot is close to what the pre-ticket-10 flipbook version showed (a human-flagged regression: the doctrine's own frameCount at the OLD higher fps made each one-shot roughly half as long as before, worsening how long a subject without idle art is actually visible during its own turn).
